title: Implement Alpaca historical bar acquisition and bounded REST fallback
description:
Implement Alpaca historical stock bar acquisition in mike_trade/market_data/alpaca_history.py and a bounded REST polling fallback in mike_trade/market_data/polling.py, with contract tests in tests/contracts/test_alpaca_history.py.

alpaca_history.py:
- Fetch historical bars for warmup and backtests through an injected HTTP client: timeframe, start/end in UTC, feed (default 'iex'), and an explicit adjustment parameter.
- Handle next_page_token pagination with a maximum page bound.
- Return immutable bar records with Decimal OHLC/VWAP, integer or Decimal volume and trade count, timezone-aware UTC bar timestamps, feed_id, and adjustment provenance (raw/split/dividend/all).
- Never silently mix adjusted and unadjusted bars, or bars from different feeds, in one result. A request whose provenance mismatches is rejected with a typed error.

polling.py:
- Implement a REST fallback poller that, on each cycle, fetches latest trade/quote/bar snapshots once per watched symbol. Use multi-symbol endpoints where available, and never fetch once per strategy or scenario.
- Enforce a configurable request-rate budget with a token bucket on the injected clock.
- Honor HTTP 429 and Retry-After with backoff.
- Bound the poll interval and the maximum symbols per cycle.
- Mark each snapshot with provider_source_ts, receive_ts, feed_id, and a source='rest_poll' provenance.
- Flag a stale snapshot when the provider timestamp has not advanced, or its age exceeds a configured threshold, rather than presenting it as fresh.
- Support bounded gap recovery: fetch missing completed bars for a gap window no larger than a configured maximum.

Tests use a fake HTTP transport with recorded or synthetic Alpaca JSON responses. They must not use the network or real credentials. Strategies must never call these modules directly; they are only for MarketDataService and backtest loaders.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/ domain/ports modules from earlier phases that define bar/quote/trade event types, the clock port, and the historical-data port (if present)
- mike_trade/config/settings modules for feed, rate-limit, and poll-interval configuration (if present)
- pyproject.toml for the approved HTTP client dependency
acceptance_criteria: alpaca_history.py follows next_page_token across pages, stops at the configured maximum page bound, and returns bars ordered by UTC timestamp; a contract test with a multi-page fake response verifies this.
Every returned bar carries Decimal OHLC/VWAP, a timezone-aware UTC timestamp, a feed_id, and an adjustment provenance value; a test asserts there are no float fields.
A request or merge that would combine different feed_ids or adjustment modes raises a typed provenance error; a negative test covers this.
polling.py issues at most one request per symbol per cycle, or one batched request for all symbols, regardless of how many strategies or scenarios consume the data; a test counts transport calls.

The token-bucket rate limiter blocks or defers requests that exceed the configured budget, and an HTTP 429 with Retry-After delays the next request by at least that duration on the injected clock; tests verify both.
Snapshots whose provider timestamp has not advanced, or whose age exceeds the stale threshold, are flagged stale; a test verifies this.
Gap recovery requests only the missing window and refuses windows larger than the configured maximum; positive and negative tests cover both.
Tests use no network access and no real or live credentials.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
use real Alpaca credentials, paid data, or network access in tests
persist raw tick or full-session data archives
run broad test suites or large backtests
